title: Count the Harvest
story: At closing time the owner asks two numbers: how many products exist, and how many units sit on the shelves.
goal: Return one row with the number of products as products and the total stock as units.

tests.label: Hidden check on other data
Hidden check on other data

hints: COUNT(*) counts rows and SUM(column) adds a column up.
Name the two results with AS products and AS units.
SELECT COUNT(*) AS products, SUM(stock) AS units FROM products;
socratic: Compare the rows you got with the rows expected. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what does your query do?
solution: SELECT COUNT(*) AS products, SUM(stock) AS units FROM products;
alt: SELECT COUNT(id) AS products, SUM(stock) AS units FROM products;
